answer:
Your records run only to mid-July 2026, so anything since then is not visible to me. Here is what I would bring up, most important first.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide may still be in your routine. In March 2026 you were in the hospital for 3 days with a sodium of 123, and the discharge papers say to STOP hydrochlorothiazide because it was the likely cause. The hospital record shows it discontinued on March 5. But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2 for 90 days and still shows it active with 2 refills left. Your family clinic's June 2026 summary also still lists it as a current medicine, and does not mention the hyponatremia. Your sodium on June 15 was low again at 134. Please check whether you are taking it. If you are, tell Dr. Marsh and the pharmacy right away. If you are not, ask for the pharmacy and clinic lists to be corrected. The reaction should also be added to your allergy and intolerance list, as lisinopril's cough already is.

2. The lung nodule has not been followed up. The CT done in the ER on October 18, 2025 (for the kidney stone) found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the right lower lung. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ended around October 18, 2026, and I find no chest CT and no mention of the nodule in your clinic notes or problem list. You have never smoked, which lowers the risk, but this follow-up is due now.

3. The thyroid recheck is missing. Your TSH was high (7.9) on March 3, 2026 with a normal free T4 (1.0). The hospital asked for both to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks. I see no repeat. Low sodium can also be linked to an underactive thyroid, so this matters for item 1 too.

4. Vaccines. Shingrix needs a second dose 2 to 6 months after the first. You had dose 1 at the pharmacy on November 8, 2025, and I find no dose 2. Your last flu shot on record was that same day, so the 2026-27 shot is not recorded yet. I also find no hepatitis B vaccine, which is generally advised for adults with diabetes under 60, and no Tdap or COVID shots. Those may simply be recorded elsewhere. Your pneumococcal (Prevnar 20) shot is done.

5. Cholesterol and statin. In September 2025 your LDL was 142, HDL 48 and triglycerides 155. No statin appears on any medication list and no repeat lipid panel appears. Adults aged 40 to 75 with diabetes are generally offered a statin, so ask whether you should start one.

6. Diabetes checks. Your A1c has come down well, 6.9 to 6.7 to 6.6 in June 2026, and your dilated eye exam in May 2026 showed no retinopathy (next due May 2027). I find no urine albumin-to-creatinine test, no documented foot exam, and no record that the diabetes education referral from September 2025 happened. Ask about all three. Your next A1c is due around December 2026, when Dr. Marsh asked to see you.

7. Kidney stone follow-up. The ER asked for a primary-care visit within a week and urology if the stone had not passed in 2 weeks. I find no record of either, nor any note on whether the stone passed. It is also absent from your clinic problem list.

8. Details that do not match across records. The aspirin reaction is described as mild in two early 2025 hospital summaries and as moderate in later ones. The lisinopril cough appears in the clinic's allergy list but not the hospital's. Worth asking everyone to align them. Because aspirin gives you hives, you were also kept off ibuprofen and ketorolac in the ER, so ask your doctor about NSAID safety.

9. Screening. Your colonoscopy on April 16, 2019 was normal with a 10-year repeat, so it is not due until about 2029. I find no mammogram or cervical screening in any of these records, so ask when they were last done.
short: Bring up: (1) hydrochlorothiazide was stopped in March 2026 for low sodium (123) but was refilled in April and is still listed as active; sodium was low again (134) in June; (2) 7 mm lung nodule from Oct 2025 needs the chest CT that was due by ~Oct 2026; (3) repeat TSH/free T4 after TSH 7.9 never recorded; (4) Shingrix dose 2, flu shot, and other vaccines; (5) no statin despite LDL 142 with diabetes; (6) urine albumin test, foot exam, diabetes education; (7) kidney stone follow-up; (8) mammogram/cervical screening not found.

knowledge.says: Thiazide diuretics are a well-known cause of low sodium, and it usually returns if the drug is restarted, so after a hospital stay for thiazide-related hyponatremia the drug is normally avoided and recorded as an adverse reaction.
knowledge.guideline: General clinical practice; no single named guideline.
